transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-21
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording link: (redacted)

Attendees:
- Jordan Nguyen (Redwood AE)
- Priya Patel (Redwood SE)
- Samir Rao (Omega, CTO)
- Elena Martinez (Omega, ML Engineer)
- Lucas Chen (Omega, Infra Lead)

---
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros — i'm jordan from redwood, ae. priya is our se, she'll jump in on latency/benchmarking questions.
[00:12] Samir: thanks jordan, samir here. short context, we're building a real-time recommendation endpoint for our ecommerce pipeline, p95 is critical, and we need to understand whether we go hosted, dedicate, or private.
[00:23] Priya: great, can you share target numbers? sometimes folks use rps and concurrency interchangeably — what's your p95 and qps goals?
[00:30] Elena: target p95 for the full response is ~250ms for short prompts (single turn, ~40-60 tokens). For larger contexts (500 tokens) we can accept up to 800ms. Concurrency we expect 200-500 concurrent active streams during peak, burst to ~800.
[00:45] Lucas: also streaming is mandatory — we stream partial recommendations to the UI for perceived latency. we benchmark tokens/sec as well because we have mixed small/long responses.
[00:58] Jordan: thanks — that helps. a couple notes on terminology: p95 here is end-to-end server-to-client with network overhead; when we do internal lab token/sec benchmarks we look at server compute p95 which is usually lower. we'll surface both.
[01:10] Priya: for hosted mode we can usually hit low p95 for small prompts, depends on model size, quantization profile, and whether prefix / kv cache hits are high. for dedicated you get predictable throughput because you reserve gpu pools. private gives you full control but add ops overhead.
[01:30] Samir: can you give a rough mapping: what models/variants would typically meet 250ms p95 for 40-60 token responses on hosted?
[01:40] Priya: rough, on modern open models — a 7B quantized variant with good kernels might do ~80-150ms server-side p95 on an A100 or H100 class instance with optimized runtime and streaming enabled. for 13B you'd see higher—250-400ms depending on prompt prep. caveat, those numbers vary by sequence length and KV cache hit rate.
[01:58] Elena: for our workload we have a high cache hit rate because many requests share prefixes — can redwood do prefix caching?
[02:06] Jordan: yes — we have automatic prefix / KV caching that reduces token generation per request when there's a shared context. that helps p95 a lot.
[02:15] Lucas: okay, when you say dedicated gpu pools, how many concurrent streams per gpu? like 1 stream per gpu or can you do batching?
[02:25] Priya: continuous batching is supported — the runtime does batching based on latency SLOs. for streaming flows we maintain KV cache and can keep many concurrent in-flight requests; exact concurrency per GPU depends on model size and sequence length. for planning we typically ask customers to run a token/sec benchmark with their payloads.
[02:43] Samir: what's the typical token/sec baseline we should expect in your hosted environment per GPU for a 7B quantized model?
[02:50] Priya: again, very workload dependent, but ballpark: 7B quantized might do 8k-15k tokens/sec sustained on an A100-80GB equivalent in our optimized runtime. 13B would be lower, maybe 3k-7k tokens/sec. those are server-side token/s for generation; end-to-end perceived throughput also depends on network and client-side streaming processing.
[03:12] Jordan: i'll note that those lab numbers are with continuous batching enabled and without network egress. we'll provide a benchmark script so you can run the same tests.
[03:22] Elena: we also want deterministic p95 at peak concurrency. hosting providers sometimes have noisy neighbors. how do you isolate noisy workloads on hosted?
[03:30] Priya: for hosted we have autoscaling and scheduling, we try to give predictable performance but if you need strict p95 SLAs you move to Dedicated where you reserve capacity. Dedicated has options for strict tenancy and capacity guarantees.
[03:44] Samir: curious about fallbacks. if dedicated pool is saturated, can traffic route to hosted fallback?
[03:49] Jordan: yes — smart routing can fallback to hosted model variants with policy controls. you can also route critical traffic to higher-tier instances and non-critical to cheaper variants.
[03:58] Lucas: on private deployments, latency should be best because it's inside our network, but we have security constraints and limited ops. what's the typical lift?
[04:06] Priya: private requires more operational ownership; we provide an appliance-like package and a control plane. for strict data residency and VPC-only access it's the right choice, but you trade maintenance and slower upgrades sometimes.
[04:16] Samir: any differences in quantization support across modes? some vendors restrict certain kernels to hosted only.
[04:22] Priya: we support the same quantization profiles across modes, but kernel availability can be hardware dependent. we'll map recommended quantization to your hardware in the PoC.
[04:32] Elena: for streaming, how do you measure p95? per-chunk or full-response? we need both.
[04:38] Priya: we capture both: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and time-to-final-token. customers often care about TTFB for perceived latency and full-response p95 for correctness windows.
[04:48] Jordan: can i ask about your conversion sensitivity? how much does 100ms move the needle for you?
[04:52] Samir: quite a bit — conversion drops noticeably above 300ms. that's why 250ms p95 target for short prompts is important.
[04:59] Jordan: understood. i'll make sure the PoC focuses on measuring both TTFB and full p95.
[05:05] Elena: about benchmarking — we'd like to run token/sec tests that include context prep, prompt templating, and a mix of short and long sequences. can you share a script?
[05:13] Priya: yes we'll send a script that reproduces our internal harness: runs warmup, measures token/sec, measures TTFB, and simulates concurrency with a ramp. includes websocket streaming client.
[05:25] Samir: will that script also measure KV cache hit effects?
[05:29] Priya: we'll include both cold and warm cache modes and instructions to pin prefixes to test cache hit ratios.
[05:35] Lucas: on networking — are you able to offer colocated endpoints in GCP in us-west1? latency to our frontends is critical.
[05:42] Jordan: yes hosted has region controls; Dedicated and Private allow you to choose region or deploy into your VPC. we'll list available zones.
[05:51] Elena: security questions: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs — can you share docs and support for bringing your own KMS?
[05:59] Jordan: yes SOC2 certs and security pack are available. BYOK with KMS/HSM is supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted supports customer-managed keys for some tiers — we'll include specifics in docs.
[06:10] Samir: any limits on streaming connections? we expect 500 concurrent websocket streams at peak.
[06:17] Priya: websocket connection scaling is part of platform; Dedicated can be sized to handle that. hosted may require shard settings; we'll validate in PoC.
[06:25] Jordan: regarding pricing for Dedicated, do you have an expected commit term and budget?
[06:31] Samir: initial pilot budget is modest — we want to validate performance. if numbers look good we'll commit to a 12-month reserved pool.
[06:38] Jordan: okay we'll prepare a couple of Dedicated sizing options with monthly and annual commit pricing.
[06:43] Elena: one of our engineers asked about measurement noise — how do you recommend we run experiments to get stable p95 numbers?
[06:49] Priya: run warmup, run multiple windows, isolate background noise, and use server-side tracing. we also recommend running both server-only microbenchmarks and full end-to-end tests. we'll include suggested scripts and statistical methods (bootstrap for p95).
[07:05] Lucas: you mentioned continuous batching — does batching increase latency variance for short prompts?
[07:11] Priya: batching trades off throughput vs latency; our runtime does workload-aware batching: it will batch when beneficial but respect latency SLOs to keep p95 targets. if you need strict low p95, we can configure reduced batch windows or use Dedicated with reserved cores to reduce batch-induced variance.
[07:30] Samir: is there a minimum commit or minimum Dedicated size?
[07:34] Jordan: typical minimum is a small reserved GPU pool equivalent to 1-2 instances; we'll include options. enterprise deals vary.
[07:41] Elena: curious about measurement units — our infra team wants to see tokens/sec, latencies, and also per-token cost estimates from the benchmark.
[07:50] Jordan: we'll include cost per 1k tokens under the tested config and an estimate for both hosted and Dedicated scenarios. cost modeling will include batching, cache hit rate assumptions, and quantization.
[08:03] Priya: another practical note: for streaming, we instrument per-chunk latency and also reconstruct end-to-end traces in the console so you can see slow hops (network vs compute).
[08:14] Samir: any gotchas we should look out for with our mixed workload (short chatty prompts and occasional long completions)?
[08:20] Priya: tune autoscaling and batching profiles, consider separating tiers by latency sensitivity (route short prompts to smaller models with low-quant latency, long completions to larger models), and use prefix caching to reduce work.
[08:35] Jordan: can you share a rough traffic pattern for the pilot? requests per second and token mix?
[08:42] Samir: expected average 150 rps, peak 450 concurrent active, 80% short (40-60 tokens), 20% long (300-800 tokens).
[08:52] Jordan: that's helpful — we'll size initial Dedicated proposals around that profile.
[08:57] Elena: for PoC, we need a reproducible dataset and test harness. samir will confirm owners.
[09:04] Samir: i'll own dataset and confirm by friday.
[09:08] Lucas: on fallback policies, can we set auto-fallback to a cheaper model when latency slips?
[09:12] Priya: yes — routing policies let you fallback to compatible model variants. you can also set canary rollouts and A/B splits.
[09:21] Jordan: any procurement or security gate keepers we should loop in early?
[09:25] Samir: procurement will get involved for Dedicated contract; security will want SOC2 + architecture review. i'll introduce them after the initial PoC.
[09:33] Elena: sample benchmark success criteria — p95 <= 250ms for short prompts 90% of test windows; sustained throughput to handle 500 concurrent with less than 10% request queuing.
[09:46] Jordan: noted — we'll aim the PoC at those metrics.
[09:50] Priya: quick technical check: do you have GPU affinity requirements or a preference for H100 vs A100?
[09:56] Lucas: we prefer H100 where available but can work with A100 if needed.
[10:01] Priya: good — H100 gives better throughput for larger models, we'll note that.
[10:07] Samir: how long does a typical PoC take? we want a 2-3 week window for benchmarking and validation.
[10:12] Jordan: typical PoC is 2-4 weeks depending on data prep. we'll do a kickoff, host tests on our hosted and a Dedicated trial cluster, and then a final report.
[10:23] Elena: for reporting, include end-to-end p95, TTFB, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and variance charts.
[10:31] Priya: yes that's standard. we'll provide dashboards and raw logs so you can reproduce metrics.
[10:36] Lucas: small question: are there any known performance regressions with the latest runtime? we run regression checks before upgrades?
[10:43] Priya: we run nightly regressions and quality checks; we also support pinned runtime versions in Dedicated/Private to avoid surprises during PoC.
[10:54] Jordan: ok we're approaching the last third — want to recap and confirm next steps.
[11:00] Jordan: action items — we'll send benchmark script and sample hosting demo, include security docs, and a Dedicated pricing sheet. Samir to confirm PoC stakeholders and dataset. schedule kickoff week of 2025-05-28, tentative.
[11:15] Samir: that sounds good. can you also include a sample websocket client for streaming?
[11:19] Priya: yes — we'll include a node and python client.
[11:23] Elena: and please add instructions to emulate prefix cache hits for the test harness.
[11:27] Priya: noted.
[11:30] Jordan: any final questions?
[11:33] Samir: no, thanks all. looking forward to the materials.
[11:36] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the materials and calendar invite for the kickoff.
[11:40] Meeting end.
